speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the timing of your symptoms: did your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness start all at once or gradually over time? Additionally, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a neuromuscular disorder. Have you experienced any recent difficulty swallowing or speaking clearly? Also, do you have any personal or family history of similar conditions?

REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electromyography (EMG): Findings indicate decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Nerve Conduction Studies: Normal conduction velocities and amplitudes; no evidence of demyelination or significant axonal loss.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.
